solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Slept outside and brought back book

indicators.note: the sleeping word goes around the other piece, so it sits outside

parts.note: kipped is informal British for slept

indicators.note: brought back means the word and is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned round

explanation.surface: Someone camped out overnight and then returned a library book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses the little word 'and'; 'book' is the definition, Stevenson's novel, not a verb meaning reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson's novel is the example of a book meant here.

clue.text: Underhand payment to attack defender

parts.note: to kick is to lash out at, a sense of attack
a back is a defensive player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A footballer is bribed to go after an opposing defender.
explanation.definitionFit: A bribe or illicit commission paid secretly is the classic underhand payment.

clue.text: See 24
Cleaned-out arbitrageur grows debts

indicators.note: cleaned out means the word arbitrageur is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: to rear is to grow or raise, as crops or children

explanation.surface: A trader wiped out by the market finds their debts piling up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaned-out' empties arbitrageur to AR, its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Money owed and overdue is a debt, so overdue sums are debts.

clue.text: Chewing pie OK for 9 composer

indicators.note: chewing mashes things up, so the letters of pie OK for are rearranged

parts.note: 9-across is the centre of gravity, and the centre of the word gravity is the letter V

explanation.surface: Someone eating pie is told it is fine to munch it for the sake of a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chewing' rearranges PIEOKFOR into PROKOFIE; V is the middle letter of the word gravity, from 9-across's answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Prokofiev, writer of Peter and the Wolf, is a Russian composer.

clue.text: Follow the master's fixed opinion

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A disciple simply adopts the teacher's firm belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine laid down and held unquestioningly is a fixed opinion.

clue.text: Intelligence taps reveal wicked woman

parts.note: wit means intelligence or quick thinking
taps are marked C for cold and H for hot

explanation.surface: Phone-tapping by intelligence services uncovers a villainess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' and 'taps' look like espionage; they are WIT and the two tap labels.
explanation.definitionFit: A hag who casts evil spells is the fairy-tale idea of a wicked woman.

clue.text: Bespectacled girls chase popular horse south of river

indicators.note: in a down answer, the pieces south of the river come below it
the girls chase the others, so they come after them

parts.note: the Wear is a river in north-east England
in means fashionable or popular
gee-gee is nursery talk for a horse
lasses is a British, chiefly northern word for girls

explanation.surface: Girls in glasses run after a favourite horse grazing south of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south of' works because this is a down answer; 'chase' means come after. The Wear is a river in County Durham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Having spectacles on one's face is exactly what bespectacled describes.

clue.text: Time fixer and journalist were let off

parts.note: a rigger fixes or fiddles results, as in rigging a vote
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A match-fixer and a reporter were released without punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'were let off' looks like an acquittal; the definition is the firing sense of let off.
explanation.definitionFit: To let off a gun or alarm is to set it going, so fired or activated.

clue.text: Tomboy cyclist's hideaway

parts.note: Sir Chris Hoy is a British Olympic track cyclist
a den is a private retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: A boyish girl hides out in a cycling champion's secret retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Hoy is a Scottish track cyclist with six Olympic golds.
explanation.definitionFit: A boisterous, unladylike girl is a hoyden, the old word for a tomboy.

clue.text: Avi, a weighty three-quarter, perhaps would be best off with a low one

definitions.text: Avi, a weighty three-quarter, perhaps would be best off with a low one

parts.words: Avi, a weighty three-quarter, perhaps would be best off with a low one
parts.note: the letters AVI sit in the middle of gravity; a rugby centre is a three-quarter, and a hefty player is steadiest with that point of balance low

explanation.surface: A heavy rugby back called Avi is advised to stay low to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Three readings: Avi is literally the middle of 'gravity'; a rugby centre is one of the three-quarters, so a weighty one is a centre with gravity; and any body is most stable when its balance point is low.
explanation.definitionFit: The balance point of a body is where its weight acts, and a low one makes for stability.

clue.text: Pitt going round a museum with nothing on, showing great self-confidence

indicators.note: nothing is put on, so it is added after the rest
Pitt's first name goes round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: Brad Pitt is the film actor
the V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A film star strides naked round a gallery, brimming with confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with nothing on' suggests nudity but adds O at the end; 'showing' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a bold show of daring, a display of great self-assurance often masking doubt.

clue.text: Excited by the fireplace

parts.note: at means beside or by, as in at the door
an ingle is an old word for a fireplace, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled just sitting beside the hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, but 'Excited' alone is the definition and the rest is wordplay; an ingle is an archaic word for a hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tingling with anticipation or thrill is how someone excited feels.

clue.text: Swindle with empty eggs the subject of a former hotline

definitions.text: the subject of a former hotline

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick

indicators.note: empty means the word eggs loses its insides, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A con trick using hollow eggs once had its own complaints line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' reduces eggs to ES. The Cones Hotline was a much-mocked 1990s UK government phone line for reporting needless roadworks cones.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic markers on British roads were the topic of John Major's short-lived complaints telephone service.

clue.text: Name homo erectus as one who didn't quite make it

definitions.text: one who didn't quite make it

parts.note: Homo erectus is an example of early man, an ancestor of modern humans

explanation.surface: Scientists propose to label a primitive human species a near-miss of evolution.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor who repeatedly comes close to success without winning is a perennial runner-up.

clue.text: Business centre hesitates about sheep numbers

indicators.note: the centre of the word Business gives its two middle letters

parts.note: a teg is a sheep in its second year
ers are the noises of someone hesitating about something

explanation.surface: A business park's boss dithers over sheep figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes IN from the middle of Business; a TEG is a young sheep, a word mainly from farming.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole numbers with no fractional part are the mathematical sense of numbers here.

clue.text: Purist Ken revolted by toll roads

indicators.note: revolted means overturned, so the letters of Purist Ken are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Ken who is a purist is disgusted by paying road tolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolted' looks like disgust; it rearranges PURISTKEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads with gates where travellers paid a fee are the historic and American toll highways.

clue.text: Curiously, top spies are the most sentimental

indicators.note: curiously means oddly, so the letters of top spies are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strangely, the best secret agents turn out to be the softest-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: Soppy is British slang for mawkish or soft, so the superlative is the most mawkish.

clue.text: New cabinet minister replaces one in shock morning after

indicators.note: the new pieces take the place of the single letter in the hair word

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it
I is the Roman numeral for one
Michael Gove was a British cabinet minister

explanation.surface: A cabinet reshuffle causes shock on the morning after the night before.
explanation.walkthrough: In HAIR, the I gives way to N plus GOVE, making HA-NGOVE-R. Michael Gove joined the UK cabinet in 2010, when this puzzle ran.
explanation.definitionFit: The headache and nausea suffered the day following heavy drinking is the morning after feeling.

clue.text: See 6
Show certain lines in reverse order at first

indicators.note: the poem sits in between those two opening letters
at first takes the opening letters of reverse and order

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A display of particular lines arranged backwards first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reverse order' looks like a reversal instruction; it only supplies the letters R and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy contest of riding and roping is staged as a public show or display.

clue.text: Noisy announcement of fresh business has American support

indicators.note: in a down answer the support goes underneath the rest
an announcement is spoken out, so the word for fresh is taken by its sound

parts.note: raw means fresh, as in uncooked; said aloud it gives the first syllable
CO is short for company, a business
US is short for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: A new firm's loud launch is backed by an American partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announcement of' takes RAW by sound only, RAU; in this down answer 'support' puts US underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Raucous means loud and harsh, as in a rowdy crowd being noisy.

clue.text: Punishes fishing boats

definitions.meaning: slaps a child as a punishment
single-masted sailing vessels used for fishing

explanation.surface: Someone disciplines fishing vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Hits as a penalty is one sense; small sailing trawlers are the nautical second sense.

clue.text: Sick at heart, mother lives for artist

indicators.note: the sickness goes into the middle of the mother word

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
ill means sick
is means exists, lives

explanation.surface: A painter's mother is unwell deep down but still alive.
explanation.walkthrough: John Everett Millais was a Victorian Pre-Raphaelite painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Millais was an English painter, so he exemplifies an artist.

clue.text: One in prison has something of a case

indicators.note: the single item goes inside the prison word

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
a means one

explanation.surface: One prisoner has something to do with a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'case' is a staircase: a single step is part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: One step of a flight is a part of a staircase, so something of a case.

clue.text: Choice small dog is swell

parts.note: plum means choice or most desirable, as in a plum job
a pup is a young, small dog

explanation.surface: A select little puppy is described as excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' looks like the adjective meaning great; it is the verb to puff out.
explanation.definitionFit: To plump up cushions is to make them fuller, to fluff them so they swell.

clue.text: Strait-laced Bill forwards new article presenting opera star

parts.note: prim means prudish or strait-laced
an ad, or advertisement, is a bill or poster
on means forwards, as in moving on
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A prudish man named Bill sends on a new piece introducing a diva.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading female singer of an opera company is its principal lady, its diva.

clue.text: Arrive before perverted fascist bloke drops first of silk undies?

indicators.note: the arriving word comes before the rest

parts.note: come means arrive

indicators.note: perverted means twisted, so the remaining letters are rearranged
drops means one letter is taken out of fascist bloke
first of picks the opening letter of silk

explanation.surface: A deviant fascist bloke drops his silk underwear on arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops first of silk' removes one S from FASCISTBLOKE; 'perverted' rearranges the rest into SBACKTOLIFE. 'undies' is read as un-dies.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as un-dies, the word means stops being dead, which is reviving.

clue.text: Heard indications at functions

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: signs are indications or pointers

explanation.surface: Listeners pick up hints at social gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'functions' looks like parties; it is the mathematical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Trigonometric ratios such as the cosine family are mathematical functions.

clue.text: Not easily convinced by working train sets

indicators.note: working means put to work, so the letters of train sets are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sceptic is unmoved by model railways in motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds out against persuasion is unyielding, hard to win over.
